title: GLM local capability profile — personalized to operator's real workload
provenance: Categories and weighting derived from mine-transcripts data/mined.jsonl (21,336 real human messages; 2,981 technical questions). Topic distribution: scillm/model-routing 464, tau/DAG+ask 406, ArangoDB memory 333, surf browser automation 203, evals/fixtures 201, JSON schema/contract 180, Python best-practices 110, git/worktree/CI 88. Near-zero pure math or general trivia. Questions authored directly (webgpt browser seat was occupied by another active lane); grading is reference+criterion for an LLM judge.

questions.input: An OpenAI-compatible LLM proxy calls a provider whose api_base is https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4 and gets HTTP 404 with body {"path":"/v4/v1/chat/completions"}. A direct curl to https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/chat/completions with the same key returns 200. Name the single root cause and the one-line fix.
questions.expected: The proxy appends /v1/chat/completions to the api_base, but z.ai's version segment is already /v4 (no /v1), so the URL becomes /api/paas/v4/v1/chat/completions and 404s. Fix: stop appending /v1 when the base path already ends in a /vN version segment (or set the client base_url to exactly .../api/paas/v4 so only /chat/completions is appended).
questions.grading: Full credit requires identifying the doubled/extra version segment (/v4 + /v1) as the cause AND a fix that removes the /v1 append; blaming the key, model name, or endpoint host is wrong.

questions.input: A model-routing proxy log shows: complete model='zai-glm-flash' -> group='zai-glm-flash', chain=['zai-glm-flash'] followed by 404 Not Found. Is the group resolution/routing broken, or is the failure downstream of routing? Justify in one sentence.
questions.expected: Routing is fine — the log shows the request correctly resolved to group 'zai-glm-flash' and its deployment; the 404 happens on the outbound HTTP call to the provider (URL/path), which is downstream of group resolution.
questions.grading: Full credit states routing succeeded and the fault is downstream (the outbound provider call/URL), not group resolution.

questions.input: Write a Python function run_handler(cmd: list[str], timeout_s: int) -> str using subprocess that runs cmd, enforces a finite timeout, raises on non-zero exit, never uses shell=True, and returns stdout. Keep it minimal.
questions.expected:
import subprocess

def run_handler(cmd: list[str], timeout_s: int) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s, check=True)
    return proc.stdout
questions.grading: Full credit: subprocess.run with a finite timeout, check=True (or explicit returncode raise), no shell=True, list argv, returns stdout.

questions.input: Write a Python helper extract_json_object(text: str) -> dict | None that returns the first top-level JSON object embedded in text (e.g. an LLM reply with prose around it). It must use the JSON parser as the grammar authority, not a regex, and return None on failure.
questions.grading: Full credit locates outer braces and hands the slice to json.loads (no regex as the parser), guards JSONDecodeError, and returns None on non-dict/failure.

eval.test_suite:
assert extract_json_object('x {"a": 1, "b": 2} y') == {"a":1,"b":2}
assert extract_json_object("no json here") is None

questions.input: Produce a strict JSON schema-shaped example object for a model-eval question bank item with fields: id (int), category (string), difficulty (one of easy|medium|hard), input (string), expected (string), grading (string). Return ONLY one example JSON object, no prose.
questions.expected: {"id": 1, "category": "code_generation", "difficulty": "easy", "input": "Write a function that returns the length of a string.", "expected": "def n(s): return len(s)", "grading": "Returns len(s) for any string."}
questions.grading: Full credit: valid JSON, exactly the six named fields, id integer, difficulty one of the enum, and no surrounding prose.

questions.input: Given this text, return ONLY JSON {"model":..,"api_base":..,"timeout":..}: 'Deployment zai-glm-flash uses model glm-5.3-flash at https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4 with a 120 second timeout.'
questions.grading: Full credit: valid JSON with model=glm-5.3-flash, api_base the exact URL, timeout=120 as a number, no extra keys or prose.

questions.input: You must choose a handler for a task DAG. The task is a single well-specified request 'summarize this 200-word changelog into 3 bullet points'. You have: a local 19GB open-weight model (cheap, ~15 tok/s, strong on single-goal extraction/summarization, weaker on multi-constraint agentic chains) and a frontier cloud model (expensive, strong everywhere). Which handler and why, in two sentences?
questions.expected: Use the local model: this is a single-goal summarization/extraction task with no multi-constraint or tool-use chain, exactly the regime where the local model performs at parity, so the frontier model's cost buys nothing here. Reserve the frontier model for multi-constraint or agentic tasks.
questions.grading: Full credit picks the local model AND justifies it by the task being single-goal summarization/extraction (the local model's strength), not by raw capability.

questions.input: Design a minimal 2-node DAG (name the nodes and the edge) that: node A asks N candidate handlers the same question concurrently, node B has one judge handler score each answer against a reference. State the topology of node A.
questions.expected: Node A = 'fan-out' (topology: concurrent) — dispatch the same prompt to all N candidate handlers in parallel; Node B = 'judge' — depends on A, receives every candidate answer plus the reference and emits a score per candidate. Edge: A -> B (B joins/consumes A's outputs).
questions.grading: Full credit: node A concurrent fan-out to N handlers, node B a judge depending on A, and a single A->B edge.

questions.input: List these five model names sorted by context window DESC. If two tie on context window, break the tie by name A-Z. Stop after the top 3 and output nothing else. Names and windows: alpha(128k), bravo(200k), charlie(200k), delta(1M), echo(32k).
questions.grading: Full credit: exactly delta, bravo, charlie in that order — delta first (1M), bravo before charlie (200k tie broken A-Z), and stops at 3 with no extra lines/prose.

questions.input: Rewrite the sentence 'the proxy appended v1 and it broke' to be exactly 8 words, in the past tense, containing the word 'router', and ending with a period. Output only the sentence.
questions.expected: The router appended v1 which broke the request.
questions.grading: Full credit: exactly 8 words, past tense, contains 'router', ends with a period, and no extra output.

questions.input: A 19GB model runs on a 24GB GPU at ~20 tok/s when a TTS service is stopped, but drops to ~12 tok/s when that service holds ~6GB of VRAM. The model still produces correct output in both cases. Explain in two sentences why throughput drops.
questions.expected: With less free VRAM, the runtime offloads some model layers to CPU/system RAM, so those layers compute far slower and the per-token latency rises, cutting throughput. Correctness is unchanged because the same weights run — only where they execute (GPU vs CPU) differs.
questions.grading: Full credit attributes the slowdown to CPU/RAM offload of layers when VRAM is scarce (hybrid split), and notes correctness is unaffected because the same weights are used.

questions.input: An eval sends prompts to a browser-backed model seat. When the browser tab is in the background, responses stall for many minutes though the process is alive. Name the mechanism and one mitigation.
questions.expected: Chrome throttles background/hidden tabs — requestAnimationFrame isn't serviced and timers are clamped when document.hidden — so the page's generation/polling loop stalls. Mitigation: keep the tab foregrounded/visible (one visible tab per window) or launch Chrome with the background-throttling flags disabled.
questions.grading: Full credit names background-tab throttling (hidden-tab rAF/timer clamping) as the mechanism and gives a real mitigation (keep tab visible, or disable throttling via launch flags).

questions.input: A pipeline kills a hung job with `pkill -f "run.sh judge-grid"` and the controlling shell itself dies with a non-zero exit. Why, and what is the safe replacement?
questions.expected: pkill -f matches against full command lines, and the pattern 'run.sh judge-grid' also matches the shell process that is currently running the pkill command (and its grep), so pkill signals itself. Safe replacement: resolve explicit PIDs first (e.g. ps/pgrep filtered to exclude the current shell and grep) and kill those PIDs individually.
questions.grading: Full credit explains pkill -f self-matches the current shell/command line and recommends explicit-PID killing (excluding self) instead.

questions.input: Write a Python one-liner style function first_nonempty(paths: list[str]) -> str | None that returns the text of the first readable, non-empty file among paths, or None. Handle read errors.
questions.grading: Full credit iterates paths, guards OSError, returns the first non-empty file's text, and returns None when none qualify.

eval.test_suite:
import tempfile, os
dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
e = os.path.join(dd,"e.txt"); open(e,"w").close()
f = os.path.join(dd,"f.txt"); open(f,"w").write("hello")
assert first_nonempty([e, f]) == "hello"
assert first_nonempty(["/no/such/path", e]) is None

questions.input: Return a comma-separated list of exactly these provider names with NO spaces, in reverse alphabetical order: zai, openai, deepseek, ollama, moonshot.
questions.grading: Full credit: exactly zai,openai,ollama,moonshot,deepseek — reverse-alphabetical, comma-separated, no spaces, no extra text.

questions.input: Fix this invalid JSON so it parses, changing as little as possible, and return ONLY the corrected JSON: {'model': 'glm-5.3-flash', 'timeout': 120, 'stream': True,}
questions.grading: Full credit: double-quoted keys/strings, Python True -> JSON true, trailing comma removed, values otherwise unchanged, no prose.
